title: Schematic Review
description: Checks a schematic before layout or release: documentation, power, grounding, component ratings, connectivity, processors, interfaces, protection, safety, test and sourcing.

items.text: Title block is complete on every sheet (project name, revision, date, author, approver)
items.hint: Check every sheet, not just the first; a missing revision on one sheet makes printed sets ambiguous.

items.text: Revision history is up to date with all changes since the last release documented
items.hint: Compare against the previous released PDF or a schematic diff; every ECO should appear.

items.text: Sheet numbers and total sheet count are correct
items.hint: Hierarchical designs often get renumbered on export; check the PDF, not just the CAD view.

items.text: All referenced documents and datasheets are at the correct revision
items.hint: Silicon errata and datasheet revisions can change pinouts, strap values or absolute maximums. Check the revision you designed against is the current one.

items.text: Schematic follows the company drafting style guide
items.hint: IPC-2612 is a useful baseline for diagramming documentation. Check symbol conventions, signal flow left to right, and readable net names.

items.text: A block diagram exists and matches the schematic hierarchy
items.hint: Reviewers should be able to trace every block (power tree, interfaces, processors) from the block diagram to a sheet.

items.text: Design requirements (inputs, outputs, environment, interfaces) are written down and traceable to the schematic
items.hint: Without a requirements list the review can only check internal consistency, not fitness for purpose.

items.text: Design notes explain non-obvious choices (strap values, deliberate DNPs, rework options, calculations)
items.hint: Put the reason next to the part; a future engineer will otherwise 'fix' a deliberate choice.

items.text: Fitted / not-fitted (DNP) and assembly-variant parts are clearly marked and match the BOM variants
items.hint: Check each variant BOM against the schematic annotation; DNP errors are a common first-build fault.

items.text: All power nets are correctly named and consistent across sheets
items.hint: Look for near-duplicates such as 3V3, +3V3 and VCC_3V3 that the tool treats as separate nets.

items.text: Every IC and polarised part is connected to a rail of the correct voltage and polarity
items.hint: Walk each IC's supply pins against its datasheet recommended operating range, including I/O-bank and analog supplies.

items.text: Inrush current is limited on high-capacitance rails and hot-pluggable inputs
items.hint: Estimate inrush from total downstream capacitance and source impedance; check it against fuse, connector and upstream supply limits.

items.text: A power tree diagram exists showing every rail, its source, converter type and load
items.hint: The power tree is the quickest way to spot missing rails, wrong sources and overloaded regulators.

items.text: Power budget is calculated for each rail, with worst-case load below the regulator rating plus margin
items.hint: Include start-up, peak and transient loads (radios transmitting, motors starting, FPGA configuration), not just typical current.

items.text: Input supply range (min, nominal, max) is defined and every input-side part is rated for the maximum
items.hint: Include tolerance of the source, cable drop and any transients the supply can produce, such as a hot-plugged adapter ringing.

items.text: Total input power and efficiency estimate fits the source capability (adapter, USB contract, PoE class, battery)
items.hint: Sum the rail budgets through each converter's efficiency at the expected load.

items.text: Behaviour on power-up, brown-out and power loss is defined for every rail
items.hint: Consider what happens when the input sags slowly: regulators dropping out of regulation, MCUs running out of spec, flash writes corrupting.

items.text: No back-powering paths exist between rails or through I/O pins when a domain is off
items.hint: Check for I/O pins driven into unpowered ICs, USB VBUS feeding back, and body diodes of load switches conducting in reverse.

items.text: Sleep / standby current budget is calculated and met, including leakage of always-on parts
items.hint: Include pull-up currents, divider currents, regulator quiescent current, LED indicators and leakage through ESD parts.

items.text: Each regulator's output voltage set point is calculated and matches the intended rail
items.hint: Recalculate from the feedback divider and the datasheet reference voltage, including resistor tolerance and reference accuracy.

items.text: Regulator input voltage range covers the full supply range, including transients and dropout at minimum input
items.hint: Check LDO dropout and buck maximum duty cycle at minimum input and maximum load.

items.text: Switching regulator inductor value, saturation current and RMS current rating suit the worst-case load
items.hint: Saturation current should exceed peak inductor current at current limit, not just at full load.

items.text: Converter input and output capacitors meet datasheet type, ESR and effective capacitance after DC bias
items.hint: Ceramic capacitors can lose most of their capacitance at rated voltage; use the manufacturer's DC-bias curves.

items.text: Loop compensation network is calculated and stable across load, input and temperature range
items.hint: Use the vendor design tool or datasheet procedure; check phase margin with real output capacitance after derating.

items.text: Soft-start time is set to limit inrush and meet any sequencing requirement
items.hint: Too fast causes inrush trips; too slow can violate a processor's maximum ramp time.

items.text: Enable, power-good and mode pins are tied or driven to a defined state
items.hint: Floating enable or mode pins can cause random start-up or unexpected light-load mode.

items.text: LDO power dissipation (Vin - Vout) x Iout is within the package's thermal capability
items.hint: Check junction temperature at maximum ambient using the datasheet thermal resistance for the real copper area.

items.text: Switching frequency is chosen to avoid sensitive bands (radio channels, audio, ADC sampling)
items.hint: Consider harmonics as well as the fundamental; spread-spectrum or synchronisation may help.

items.text: Ground nets are clearly defined (e.g. AGND, DGND, PGND, chassis) and separated only where there is a reason
items.hint: Each separate ground net needs a documented purpose and a defined connection point.

items.text: Ground connections are present on all ICs and connectors
items.hint: Include exposed pads and thermal pads that the datasheet requires to be grounded.

items.text: Where ground nets are split, they are joined at exactly one intended point
items.hint: A single solid ground plane is often preferred over splits; if grounds are split, check there is one deliberate tie (net tie or 0 ohm) and no accidental second path.

items.text: Return paths for high-current loads do not share a path with sensitive analog or sensing grounds
items.hint: Annotate high-current returns so the layout engineer routes them separately (e.g. Kelvin connections).

items.text: Shield and cable-screen terminations are defined (chassis, ground, RC, or floating) with a reason
items.hint: Decide this at schematic stage; changing it later usually needs a respin.

items.text: Ground references across board-to-board and cable interfaces have enough ground pins for the return current
items.hint: Count ground pins against the signal and power pins; too few causes ground bounce and EMC problems.

items.text: Every supply pin has decoupling per the datasheet recommendation
items.hint: Verify capacitor values and note any placement requirement for the layout engineer; a common rule of thumb is one small ceramic per supply pin.

items.text: Bulk capacitance is adequate for each power rail
items.hint: Size it for load steps and source impedance; check effective capacitance after DC bias.

items.text: Decoupling capacitor voltage rating and dielectric are suitable after DC-bias derating
items.hint: Small 0402/0201 high-value ceramics can lose most of their capacitance at rated voltage.

items.text: Total capacitance on each rail is within the regulator's stable range and the source's hot-plug limits
items.hint: Excess capacitance can destabilise LDOs, upset soft-start, or exceed USB and hot-swap limits.

items.text: Analog, PLL and reference supply pins have filtering per datasheet (ferrite, RC or dedicated LDO)
items.hint: Check the ferrite or resistor does not drop too much voltage at the pin's maximum current.

items.text: Ferrite-bead filters are checked for resonance with the downstream capacitance
items.hint: An LC formed by a bead and ceramic capacitors can peak and amplify noise; add damping if needed.

items.text: Power distribution network target impedance is analysed for high-current, fast-transient rails
items.hint: Large FPGAs and SoCs often need a PDN analysis or the vendor's decoupling calculator rather than rules of thumb.

items.text: All component values (R, L, C) are correct per design calculations
items.hint: Spot-check calculated values against the parts in the BOM, including unit prefixes (k vs M, n vs u).

items.text: Capacitor and passive voltage ratings have adequate margin per the derating policy
items.hint: Use the company derating policy; 2x working voltage for ceramics is a common rule of thumb. Tantalum and electrolytic types have their own derating rules.

items.text: Power ratings of resistors and inductors are sufficient with derating applied
items.hint: Check pulse and surge ratings too, not only steady-state dissipation, for inrush, sense and snubber resistors.

items.text: Component tolerances are acceptable for the application
items.hint: Do a worst-case or tolerance stack-up on dividers, references, filters and timing circuits.

items.text: Ferrite bead impedance and current ratings are verified for every use
items.hint: Impedance drops with DC current; check the bead curve at the actual load current.

items.text: No part is operated beyond its absolute maximum ratings in any operating mode
items.hint: Include start-up, shutdown, fault and transient conditions as well as normal operation.

items.text: Semiconductor current, voltage and power ratings have margin per the derating policy
items.hint: MOSFETs, diodes and transistors should be checked at maximum junction temperature, not 25 °C.

items.text: Every part's operating temperature range covers the product's environment
items.hint: Commercial-grade parts may not cover outdoor, automotive or in-enclosure temperatures.

items.text: Automotive-qualified (AEC-Q) parts are used where required
items.hint: Check each part number's qualification, not just the family; suffixes often distinguish grades.

items.text: Capacitor dielectric suits the function (C0G/NP0 for timing and filters, X7R/X5R for decoupling)
items.hint: Class II dielectrics drift with voltage, temperature and age; they are unsuitable for precision timing or filters.

items.text: Capacitor ripple-current ratings are adequate in converters, motor drives and bulk positions
items.hint: Calculate RMS ripple current and compare with the rating at operating temperature and frequency.

items.text: Ceramic capacitors in high-flex or high-voltage positions use flex-term or suitable package choices
items.hint: Large ceramics near board edges, connectors or mounting holes are prone to flex cracking that can short rails.

items.text: ERC (Electrical Rules Check) has been run with zero errors
items.hint: Run ERC on the final schematic, not an earlier save; errors waived in the tool still count until justified.

items.text: No pin is left unconnected unless the datasheet allows it and it is intentionally marked no-connect
items.hint: Check unused inputs on logic, op-amps and comparators; floating CMOS inputs cause extra current and erratic behaviour.

items.text: No-connect markers are placed on all unused pins intended to be left open
items.hint: Explicit markers show the omission was deliberate and keep ERC clean.

items.text: Power pins (VCC, GND) of all ICs are explicitly connected - none hidden or implicit
items.hint: Hidden power pins in library symbols can connect to the wrong net name; show them on the symbol.

items.text: Differential pair nets are correctly paired and labelled (e.g. USB_D+/USB_D-)
items.hint: Use consistent _P/_N or +/- suffixes so layout tools recognise the pairs.

items.text: Bus connections and wire junctions are unambiguous (no four-way junctions)
items.hint: Use offset T-junctions so a dot is never missed or mis-printed.

items.text: Net labels are consistent and unique - no accidental shorts or opens from duplicate or misspelled labels
items.hint: Review the netlist for nets with a single connection and for unexpectedly merged nets.

items.text: All connectors have correct pin count, pinout and mating connector called out
items.hint: Check against the mating board or cable drawing, watching for pin-1 orientation and mirror-image errors.

items.text: Every ERC warning is reviewed and either fixed or waived with a recorded reason
items.hint: Unreviewed ERC warnings often hide single-pin nets and conflicting drivers.

items.text: Symbol pin numbers match the footprint and the datasheet pinout for every part
items.hint: Pay special attention to new or self-made library parts, multi-package parts and SOT-23 transistors whose pinouts vary by vendor.

items.text: Multi-part symbols have every unit placed, including power units
items.hint: An unplaced unit of a quad op-amp or a power-only section leaves pins unconnected without an ERC error in some tools.

items.text: Signal direction (TX/RX, MOSI/MISO, CTS/RTS) is correct across every interface
items.hint: Crossovers are a frequent first-build fault; label nets from the controller's point of view.

items.text: Netlist has been compared against the previous revision and every difference is intended
items.hint: A netlist diff catches accidental edits that a visual review misses.

items.text: All processor supply pins, including analog, I/O-bank, core and backup domains, are connected per datasheet
items.hint: Check against the datasheet pin table, not the symbol; some packages bond out extra supply pins.

items.text: Boot-mode and configuration straps are set to the intended state
items.hint: Consider leaving a way to override straps for development (jumper or test pad). Check strap pins that double as GPIOs are not pulled the wrong way by external loads at reset.

items.text: Pin multiplexing is validated in the vendor pin tool, with no function conflicts
items.hint: Export the pin assignment from the vendor tool and compare against the schematic net names.

items.text: Peripheral pin choices respect alternate-function, timer and ADC-channel limits
items.hint: Check that ADC inputs are on ADC-capable pins, PWM outputs on suitable timer channels and that 5 V-tolerant pins are used where needed.

items.text: Internal regulator pins (VCAP, VDDCORE etc.) have the capacitor value and type the datasheet specifies
items.hint: Missing or wrong core regulator capacitors are a common cause of a board that will not start.

items.text: GPIO current per pin and per port is within datasheet limits
items.hint: Directly driven LEDs, buzzers and relays can exceed total port current.

items.text: Pins that are high-impedance or toggling during reset do not cause unwanted actions on driven loads
items.hint: Motor enables, heaters, relays and power switches need a defined safe state via pull resistors until firmware takes control.

items.text: External memory (flash, EEPROM) interface, voltage and boot source are compatible with the processor
items.hint: Check boot ROM support for the chosen flash type, interface width and voltage.

items.text: FPGA configuration mode, configuration memory and done/init signals are connected per vendor guidance
items.hint: Check mode pins, config memory size for the bitstream, and pull-ups on open-drain config signals.

items.text: FPGA I/O-bank voltages match the I/O standards assigned to each bank
items.hint: Run the vendor pin planner with I/O standards set and check its report.

items.text: DDR memory interface pinout, termination and reference voltage follow the controller vendor's guidelines
items.hint: Byte-lane swaps and bit swaps must follow the controller's rules; check VTT and VREF supplies.

items.text: Clock sources and frequencies match MCU, FPGA and interface requirements
items.hint: Check accuracy and jitter requirements of interfaces such as USB, Ethernet and radios, not just nominal frequency.

items.text: Crystal load capacitors are calculated from the crystal's specified load capacitance and stray capacitance
items.hint: Use the crystal datasheet CL and an estimate of stray capacitance; check drive level and the oscillator's gain margin.

items.text: Reset circuitry (supervisor IC or RC) is appropriate and reset polarity is correct
items.hint: Check threshold relative to the minimum operating voltage of every part held in reset.

items.text: Power sequencing requirements are met (where applicable)
items.hint: Check order, ramp time and maximum delay between rails against each datasheet, including power-down sequencing.

items.text: Clock fan-out, termination and drive strength suit each load
items.hint: Check that one oscillator output is not driving too many loads or a long run without termination.

items.text: Low-frequency (32.768 kHz) crystal is compatible with the oscillator's drive level and ESR limits
items.hint: Low-power oscillators are very sensitive to crystal ESR and load capacitance; use the vendor's recommended crystal list.

items.text: Reset is held until all supplies and clocks are stable
items.hint: Check supervisor delay against the slowest rail and oscillator start-up time.

items.text: Watchdog configuration (internal or external) is defined, including how it is disabled for debug
items.hint: External watchdogs that cannot be disabled make debugging with breakpoints difficult.

items.text: Enable and power-good chain implements the required sequence with no circular dependency
items.hint: Trace each enable back to its source; a regulator enabled by a rail it powers will never start.

items.text: Jitter budget for high-speed SerDes and data-converter clocks is met by the chosen reference
items.hint: Compare the oscillator phase-noise or jitter spec with the SerDes or ADC requirement over the specified integration band.

items.text: Op-amp feedback network values are verified for gain, bandwidth and stability
items.hint: Check gain-bandwidth product against the closed-loop gain and signal bandwidth.

items.text: Op-amp outputs do not drive an unsupported capacitive load directly
items.hint: Use an isolation resistor or a part rated for the load; cable and ADC input capacitance count.

items.text: ADC/DAC reference voltage source is stable and low-noise
items.hint: Check reference accuracy, drift and its ability to supply the ADC's dynamic reference current.

items.text: Anti-aliasing filters are present and correctly designed before ADC inputs
items.hint: The filter should attenuate content above half the sample rate enough for the required accuracy.

items.text: Sensitive analog signals are marked for separation from noisy digital and power circuits
items.hint: Mark sensitive nets and add layout notes so they are kept away from switch nodes and clocks.

items.text: Op-amp input and output common-mode ranges cover the actual signal swing on the chosen rails
items.hint: Non rail-to-rail parts on single low supplies often clip near the rails.

items.text: ADC driver can settle the ADC sampling capacitor within the acquisition time
items.hint: Check the driver's bandwidth and the RC between driver and ADC per the ADC datasheet.

items.text: Analog inputs are protected against overvoltage without degrading accuracy
items.hint: Clamp diodes and series resistors add leakage and error; include them in the error budget.

items.text: Error budget (offset, gain, noise, drift, resistor tolerance) meets the measurement accuracy requirement
items.hint: A worst-case or RSS budget should exist for each precision measurement chain.

items.text: Sensor excitation, bias and ratiometric referencing are defined
items.hint: Ratiometric measurement removes reference error; check the excitation source and the ADC reference share a source where intended.

items.text: Current-sense resistor and amplifier are sized for range, resolution and Kelvin connection
items.hint: Mark the Kelvin sense connections on the schematic so layout does not share them with the current path.

items.text: Audio path gain staging leaves headroom at every stage up to the codec or amplifier full-scale level
items.hint: Check maximum signal at each stage against the supply and the codec full-scale level.

items.text: Audio outputs have DC blocking and pop/click suppression at power-up and power-down
items.hint: Check coupling-capacitor charging behaviour and the codec or amplifier mute sequence.

items.text: RF matching networks and antenna feed follow the radio vendor's reference design
items.hint: Include tuning component placeholders (pi network) so the match can be adjusted after layout.

items.text: Radio module or RF IC supply decoupling and filtering follow the reference design
items.hint: Radios are sensitive to supply ripple; check transmit current peaks against the regulator and bulk capacitance.

items.text: Pull-up or pull-down resistors are present on all open-drain / open-collector outputs
items.hint: Check interrupt, alert, fault and power-good lines as well as the obvious buses.

items.text: Series termination resistors are included on high-speed lines where required
items.hint: Typical candidates are clock lines, fast SPI and parallel buses with long runs.

items.text: Logic voltage levels are compatible between every driver and receiver
items.hint: Check VOH/VOL against VIH/VIL at the actual supply voltages, including 5 V-tolerance of inputs.

items.text: Level translators are included wherever mixed-voltage interfaces need them
items.hint: Auto-direction translators misbehave with strong pull-ups or with push-pull and open-drain on the same line; check the part suits the bus.

items.text: Each I2C bus has a single set of pull-ups sized for bus capacitance and speed
items.hint: Pull-ups on modules and breakout boards add in parallel; size per the I2C specification's rise-time method.

items.text: SPI chip-select lines are correctly connected with the right polarity and no shared-CS conflicts
items.hint: Add pull-ups on chip selects so devices stay deselected while the controller is in reset.

items.text: I2C addresses on each bus are unique, including address straps and module defaults
items.hint: Make an address table per bus; address-select pins must not be left floating.

items.text: USB data lines, VBUS sensing and CC/ID pins are connected per the USB connector type and role
items.hint: USB-C needs CC resistors or a controller per its role; check VBUS detection and the ID or CC configuration.

items.text: Ethernet PHY strapping, magnetics and termination follow the PHY reference design
items.hint: Check centre-tap connection (voltage-mode vs current-mode PHY) and the Bob Smith termination network.

items.text: AC-coupling capacitors are present on high-speed serial links where the standard requires them, on the correct side
items.hint: PCIe, SATA, DisplayPort and similar links specify which end the capacitors sit on.

items.text: High-speed differential pairs have impedance and length-matching requirements recorded for layout
items.hint: Record target impedance and skew limits in schematic notes or net classes.

items.text: Polarity swaps and lane swaps on high-speed links are permitted by both ends
items.hint: Some interfaces allow P/N inversion or lane reversal; others do not.

items.text: Display and touch interfaces (MIPI, LVDS, RGB, SPI) match the panel datasheet pinout and voltage
items.hint: Check backlight driver current and voltage, panel power sequence and the FPC pinout orientation.

items.text: Interrupt and wake-up lines are routed to wake-capable pins
items.hint: Not all GPIOs can wake the processor from its deepest sleep mode.

items.text: ESD and transient protection is present at every external interface
items.hint: List every connector, button and exposed conductive part and confirm each has protection.

items.text: Over-voltage protection is present on all external-facing inputs
items.hint: Include miswiring to other supply voltages the product might plausibly see.

items.text: Over-current protection (fuse, PTC or current limiter) is present on power inputs and outputs
items.hint: Check the fuse rating against normal load, inrush I2t and the wiring or connector it protects.

items.text: Reverse polarity protection is implemented where applicable
items.hint: Check the protection device's loss at full load and its voltage rating.

items.text: TVS and clamp diode ratings (working voltage, clamping voltage, capacitance) suit each protected signal
items.hint: Working voltage must exceed the normal signal level; clamping voltage must be below the protected IC's limits; capacitance must suit high-speed lines.

items.text: Chassis ground and protective earth connections are correctly handled for safety-critical designs
items.hint: Check the earth bond path and how chassis is connected to circuit ground (direct, RC or isolated).

items.text: Outputs that drive off-board loads survive a short circuit to ground and to supply
items.hint: Check output drivers, power outputs and sensor supplies for short-circuit protection.

items.text: Common-mode chokes or filters are provided on cables that may radiate or receive interference
items.hint: Consider footprints for EMC fixes even if fitted as 0 ohm initially.

items.text: Input power filtering meets conducted-emissions targets for switching converters
items.hint: Plan for an input pi filter with damping; include footprints for tuning during pre-compliance.

items.text: Automotive supply inputs withstand load dump, reverse battery and transient pulses for the required standard
items.hint: Check the protection against the transient levels in the applicable automotive standard (ISO 7637 / ISO 16750 style).

items.text: Surge and EFT protection on long-cable industrial interfaces is rated for the required immunity levels
items.hint: Industrial I/O, RS-485 and 24 V inputs typically need surge-rated TVS and series impedance.

items.text: Inductive loads have flyback or clamp protection
items.hint: Relays, solenoids and long cables need a clamp; check its effect on release time.

items.text: Battery protection (over-charge, over-discharge, over-current, short circuit) is provided in the pack or on the board
items.hint: Confirm which protections the pack provides and which the board must add; do not assume.

items.text: Charge voltage and current settings match the cell chemistry and manufacturer limits
items.hint: Check the charge termination voltage, charge current and pre-charge current against the cell datasheet.

items.text: Charging is inhibited outside the cell's allowed temperature range
items.hint: Check the thermistor type and the charger's temperature thresholds match the cell datasheet.

items.text: Battery connector is keyed and polarity-protected against incorrect insertion
items.hint: Consider what happens if a user forces a reversed connector or a wrong pack.

items.text: Fuel gauging or voltage monitoring is accurate enough for the state-of-charge requirement
items.hint: Voltage-only estimates are poor for flat discharge curves; consider a fuel gauge IC.

items.text: Deep-discharge and shelf-life behaviour (ship mode, leakage) is defined
items.hint: Leakage through dividers and always-on parts can flatten a battery in storage; consider ship mode.

items.text: Load sharing / power-path handles a dead or missing battery while external power is present
items.hint: Check the system can boot from external power with a deeply discharged battery.

items.text: Coin cell or backup battery circuits prevent reverse charging of primary cells
items.hint: Primary lithium cells must not be charged; check diode or series resistor protection per cell datasheet.

items.text: Power MOSFETs / IGBTs have voltage, current and SOA margin for the worst-case operating point
items.hint: Check SOA for linear operation during switching, start-up and fault conditions.

items.text: Gate drive voltage, current and gate resistors suit the switches and the target switching speed
items.hint: Check gate charge against driver capability and the bootstrap supply capacity at low duty cycle.

items.text: Dead time and shoot-through protection are defined for half-bridges
items.hint: Set dead time in hardware or document the firmware requirement and the driver's minimum.

items.text: Regenerative energy from motor braking is handled (clamp, brake resistor, or supply absorption)
items.hint: Regeneration can pump the DC bus above component ratings, especially when the supply cannot sink current.

items.text: Motor current sensing covers the full range with adequate bandwidth for control and protection
items.hint: Check amplifier common-mode range for high-side or in-phase sensing and blanking at switching edges.

items.text: Hardware over-current or short-circuit shutdown responds faster than the switch can be damaged
items.hint: Firmware-only protection is usually too slow for a shorted output.

items.text: DC-bus capacitance and ripple-current rating are adequate for the switching current
items.hint: Check capacitor RMS ripple current at maximum load and temperature.

items.text: Snubbers or clamps limit switching overshoot to within device ratings
items.hint: Leave footprints for RC snubbers if the layout parasitics are not yet known.

items.text: Motor outputs are in a safe state at power-up, reset and fault
items.hint: Driver enables should be pulled to the disabled state independently of firmware.

items.text: Encoder, Hall and position-sensor inputs have filtering and protection suitable for motor noise
items.hint: Motor cables carry large common-mode noise; check pull-ups, filtering and ESD on sensor inputs.

items.text: Insulation class and isolation barriers are identified on the schematic
items.hint: Mark the primary/secondary boundary and the required insulation level (basic, supplementary, reinforced) on each barrier.

items.text: Parts bridging the isolation barrier (transformers, optocouplers, Y-capacitors, isolators) carry the required safety ratings
items.hint: Check each part's certification and rated insulation voltage against the applicable safety standard.

items.text: Creepage and clearance requirements are recorded for layout per the applicable safety standard
items.hint: Write the required distances into layout notes or rules; the schematic is where the requirement originates.

items.text: Mains input has a correctly rated fuse in the line conductor
items.hint: Check breaking capacity and voltage rating as well as current; position per the safety standard.

items.text: Mains input has surge protection (MOV or similar) rated for the product's mains range
items.hint: Check MOV rating for the highest mains voltage and its failure mode protection.

items.text: Mains inrush current is limited to suit the fuse, switch and upstream supply
items.hint: Use an NTC, active inrush limiter or the converter's soft-start; check behaviour on a hot restart when an NTC is still warm.

items.text: X and Y capacitors are safety-rated parts of the correct class
items.hint: Check the X/Y subclass and certification marks against the position and working voltage.

items.text: Total Y-capacitance and other leakage paths keep touch and patient leakage current within the allowed limit
items.hint: Leakage limits for medical equipment are much stricter than for IT equipment; calculate at maximum mains voltage and frequency.

items.text: Bleed resistors discharge X capacitors and high-voltage bulk capacitors to a safe level in the required time
items.hint: Check the resistor voltage rating; use series resistors to share voltage.

items.text: Medical applied parts have the required means of patient protection and isolation
items.hint: Confirm the applied-part classification and the number of means of protection with the regulatory lead.

items.text: Single-fault conditions have been considered for safety-critical circuits
items.hint: Short or open each critical component in turn and confirm the product remains safe.

items.text: Power dissipation is estimated for every significant part at worst-case load and ambient
items.hint: List each part over a few hundred milliwatts with its estimated junction temperature (rule of thumb threshold; adjust per project).

items.text: Parts relying on copper area or heatsinks have thermal requirements noted for layout
items.hint: Note the required copper area, thermal vias or heatsink so the assumption survives into layout.

items.text: Thermal shutdown or temperature monitoring is provided where overheating is possible
items.hint: A thermistor or temperature sensor near hot parts allows firmware derating.

items.text: Temperature-sensitive parts (references, crystals, sensors, electrolytics) are noted to be kept away from heat sources
items.hint: Add placement notes so layout keeps them away from regulators and power stages.

items.text: Touch-temperature limits for accessible surfaces are considered in the dissipation budget
items.hint: Enclosure surface temperature can limit allowable dissipation more than component ratings.

items.text: Test points are provided on all critical nets (power rails, key signals)
items.hint: Include every rail, reset, clocks, boot straps and key communication buses.

items.text: JTAG / SWD / debug header is present with the correct pinout
items.hint: Check against the debug probe's pinout, including reference voltage and reset pins.

items.text: Reference designators are unique and follow the naming convention
items.hint: Re-annotation after copy-paste often creates gaps or duplicates.

items.text: BOM is generated and cross-checked against the schematic
items.hint: Check quantities, DNP fields and manufacturer part numbers against the schematic values.

items.text: Footprint assignments are reviewed for every component - correct package selected
items.hint: Check package variants of the same part number (e.g. QFN vs SOIC) and pin-1 orientation.

items.text: Board-level notes and assembly instructions are included on the schematic
items.hint: Include special processes such as selective solder, conformal coat masks or press-fit parts.

items.text: Schematic PDF and netlist are exported at the final revision, with file names reflecting the revision
items.hint: Check the PDF is searchable and the revision in the file name matches the title block.

items.text: Programming and debug access works in production as well as development
items.hint: Production programming may use pogo pins or a fixture rather than a header; check the access plan.

items.text: A debug UART or log output is available
items.hint: A spare UART on test pads is invaluable during bring-up and field returns.

items.text: Power rails can be isolated for bring-up (0 ohm links, jumpers or current-measure points)
items.hint: Being able to bring up rails one at a time and measure current saves boards during first power-on.

items.text: Production test coverage is defined and test access exists for each tested function
items.hint: Agree the test strategy (ICT, flying probe, functional test) with the manufacturer.

items.text: Unique serialisation, calibration storage and MAC/ID provisioning are planned
items.hint: Decide where calibration constants and unique IDs live and how production writes them.

items.text: All components are from the approved vendor list or justified exceptions are documented
items.hint: New vendors need a quality and supply review before production.

items.text: Obsolete or end-of-life parts are flagged and replaced
items.hint: Check lifecycle status with the distributor or a lifecycle tool, including NRND (not recommended for new design) status.

items.text: Single-source parts are identified and have a mitigation plan or approved alternative
items.hint: List alternates for passives and common parts; flag single-source ICs to the project lead.

items.text: Stock and lead time are checked for every part needed for the next build
items.hint: Check availability at the build quantity, not just whether one is in stock.

items.text: Environmental compliance (RoHS, REACH and any customer-specific substance lists) is confirmed for all parts
items.hint: Check part compliance data, not just the family claim.

items.text: Parts with moisture sensitivity or special handling are identified for the assembler
items.hint: MSL ratings and special handling notes help prevent assembly defects.
